claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning a formal assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to ask you about your child or children:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

Please let me know:
- The name of each child
- Their date of birth (or current age)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 18 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, who is 18 years old**. That's helpful context.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the 16-19 age category. For young people in this age range, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

Let me ask you: **Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

This could include:
- Full-time schooling (secondary or higher education)
- Full-time vocational training
- Apprenticeships or other approved training schemes

Please let me know his current status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training right now. He finished school and he's just been at home, not really doing anything at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex is 18 and not currently in any education or training.

Let me navigate through the eligibility rules with this information:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask a follow-up question. Since Alex has finished school but isn't in education or training, I need to check: **When did Alex finish school?**

Specifically, was it within the last 20 weeks? This matters because there's a special extension period for young people who have recently left education.

Please provide:
- The approximate date he finished school (or how long ago that was)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He finished back in the summer - that was quite a while ago now, probably about 8 or 9 months ago.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex finished school about 8 or 9 months ago, that's well beyond the 20-week extension period that would apply to young people who have recently left education.

Let me navigate to the next step:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the eligibility rules, **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**The Rule:** Child Benefit can be claimed for:
- Children under 16, OR
- Young people aged 16-19 who are in approved full-time education or training

**Your Situation:** Alex is 18 years old and is not currently in approved education or training. He finished school about 8-9 months ago, which is well beyond the 20-week extension period that would apply if he had only recently left education.

**What This Means:** Since Alex doesn't meet the qualifying criteria, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

**Important Note:** If circumstances change and Alex enters full-time education or approved training before his 20th birthday, you may be able to claim at that point - so it's worth reconsidering this if his situation changes.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about the rules, or are you asking about any other children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's all I needed to know. Thank you for explaining it to me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the rules for you.

To summarize: since Alex is 18 and not currently in education or training, he doesn't qualify as a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes. However, remember that if his situation changes and he starts full-time education or approved training before his 20th birthday, you may be able to claim at that point.

If you have any other questions in the future about Child Benefit or need help with a different situation, feel free to ask.

Best of luck, and take care!
